strongest_angle: The October 2026 theft of a newly unveiled heritage plaque at Portchester Castle highlights the erasure of 2,500 African-Caribbean prisoners of war brought to Britain in 1796.

key_facts.fact: A heritage plaque commemorating 2,500 African Caribbean men, women, and children brought to Britain as prisoners of war was unveiled at Portchester Castle on Friday 9 October 2026.
Castle staff discovered that the plaque and a gate padlock had been removed on Wednesday 14 October 2026, just five days after the unveiling ceremony.
The 1796 prisoner group represents one of the largest known arrivals of African-Caribbean people in Britain before the Windrush era.
Portchester Castle is located in Hampshire, where the memorial plaque was installed and subsequently stolen.
